findings.evidence: design.md, 'Evidence source availability': "The Requirement review additionally reads the pre-authoring state; if it cannot be read, that source is reported the same way." In template/scripts/requirement_retrospective.py, review-path emits `evidence_sources: agent_friction.evidence_source_status()`, which only covers `friction-log`. `_explain_signals` checks the same single source. No pre-authoring source is read or gated.
findings.summary: The design says the Requirement review also reads the pre-authoring state and reports it as an evidence source if it is unreadable. The candidate does not implement this.

findings.evidence: docs/engineering/agent-workflow.md line 43 and the matching line in template/docs/engineering/agent-workflow.md.jinja say `--result none` needs only "every current-task high-signal lifecycle failure" to have a disposition, and that "`--lifecycle-disposition` is for the resolved/already-recorded cases". The new text says all mandatory signals need a link or disposition, the flag is now `--disposition`, and `expected-behavior` is accepted.
findings.summary: The same docs paragraph still describes the old, narrower disposition contract. It contradicts the new paragraphs added directly above it.
